about: But That's None of My Business shows Kermit the Frog by a sunny window, holding a clear mug of Lipton tea with the yellow tag dangling and taking a slow sip, eyes turned away. It is the picture of someone who has just said something pointed and is now pretending it was not about anyone. Captions make a petty, passive-aggressive observation about a person or group, then close with "but that's none of my business". The joke is that Kermit very obviously made it his business and is enjoying the tea, in both senses, while acting innocent.
origin: The image comes from a Lipton tea commercial featuring Kermit. Instagram users began posting it with shady captions in early 2014, and the "none of my business" tagline turned it into one of the most popular reaction images of that year.
usage:
The top box holds the shade: a sly observation about something someone does, like "you post gym pics every day but can't help me move". The bottom box is nearly always "but that's none of my business".

The tone should be gossipy and specific, never outright angry, so the polite sign-off contrasts with the jab. It is perfect for roommates, coworkers, fandom drama and sports rivalries.
